clue.text: To beg is to that extent legal

parts.note: so, as in 'so far and no further', means to that extent
licit means lawful, permitted

explanation.surface: Someone argues that begging is only as lawful as far as it goes.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask earnestly or plead for something, a synonym of begging.

clue.text: Animal is picked up by this untidy person

definitions.text: Animal is picked up by this

explanation.surface: An untidy person picks up an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cat or dog may be lifted by the loose skin at the back of its neck; the word also means a shabby, unkempt individual.

clue.text: Bound to follow flower arrangement in one's spare time

indicators.note: the word for bound comes after the flower arrangement

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
sure means bound, as in 'bound to happen'

explanation.surface: Someone is certain to take up flower arranging as a hobby.
explanation.definitionFit: Leisure is free time away from work.

clue.text: A crass and extraordinary prophetess

indicators.note: extra-ordinary suggests out of the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coarse and remarkable seer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extraordinary' rearranges A CRASS AND.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend this Trojan princess foretold the future but was never believed.

clue.text: My plans are upset — there's the problem about rent!

explanation.surface: Someone whose plans collapse blames a dispute over the rent.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'rent' as torn: the problem concerns something ripped.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial exclamation means everything is ruined; literally it points out that something has been ripped.

clue.text: In school in France, what a crushing retort!

indicators.note: the French word goes in, enclosed by the abbreviation for school

parts.note: quel is French for what

explanation.surface: An exclamation at a stinging comeback delivered in a French classroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase is a foreign-language leaf: setters often borrow simple French words such as quel, le or et.
explanation.definitionFit: A squelch is a remark that silences or flattens someone, the same thing as a put-down that crushes.

clue.text: Visit the bishop's office

explanation.surface: Call on the bishop at his workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: To see someone is to visit them; a bishop's see is his diocese or seat of office.

clue.text: We heard you lock up the Hittite

indicators.note: what we hear is a sound, so the word is taken by its sound alone

parts.note: the letter U sounds like you

indicators.note: in a down entry the word is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a lock is a tress of hair

explanation.surface: An eavesdropper reports someone imprisoning a Hittite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses HAIR to RIAH. Uriah the Hittite was the soldier King David sent to his death in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Old Testament this soldier, husband of Bathsheba, is known by that epithet.

clue.text: Novice wants to look round a lot of ships

indicators.note: the look goes round the other letters

parts.note: to leer is to look slyly
taken as written
RN, the Royal Navy, is a large number of ships

explanation.surface: A beginner wants to inspect a fleet.
explanation.walkthrough: RN (Royal Navy) standing for 'a lot of ships' is a common crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: A learner is someone still being taught, a beginner.

clue.text: Country house had a nice layout

indicators.note: a layout is an arrangement, so the letters are set out anew

explanation.surface: A rural residence was attractively arranged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layout' rearranges HAD A NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate house in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Bring back control by the civil power

parts.note: a rein is a means of control, as in 'keep a tight rein'
the state is the civil authority of a nation

explanation.surface: A call to restore authority to the government.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinstate is to restore someone or something to a former position, a synonym of returning it.

clue.text: Is a bill in the name of Newton?

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
an account, abbreviated AC, is a bill

explanation.surface: A question whether an invoice has been made out to someone called Newton.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Isaac Newton is the physicist, so his given name defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Newton the scientist's first name was this biblical forename.

clue.text: Rural deity given a list of animals

parts.note: a faun is a Roman god of the countryside, half man, half goat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A country god is handed an inventory of beasts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names the animal life of a region, and also a catalogue or treatise listing those creatures.

clue.text: Magical transformation as each angel sloughs skin

indicators.note: shedding its skin, the phrase 'as each angel' loses its outer letters, leaving the run within

explanation.surface: Each angel changes form by shedding its skin, like a snake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sloughs skin' strips the first and last letters off the phrase 'as each angel'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Ariel's song in The Tempest, describing a rich and strange alteration; it now means any profound change.

clue.text: A girl takes in first woman and then fellows — quite a feat!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the girl encloses the other words

parts.note: a chit is a young girl
Eve was the first woman in Genesis
men are fellows

explanation.surface: A girl accommodates Eve and then some men, which is remarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chit' is an old word for a young, often cheeky, girl.
explanation.definitionFit: An achievement is something accomplished with effort, a notable deed.

clue.text: How .Ted, a toddler, falls asleep

indicators.note: the words tumble over, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Describes how a little boy called Ted drops off to sleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'falls' looks like part of 'falls asleep', but it is the anagram signal; the stray full stop before 'Ted' is a printing mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sound asleep is unaware of everything around them, the idiom for deep slumber.

clue.text: After law is broken left the force

indicators.note: broken, the words fall apart and their letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: Once the law is broken, someone quits the police.
explanation.walkthrough: 'force' is a northern English word for a waterfall, not the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Lake District and Yorkshire, a force is a cascade, from Old Norse foss.

clue.text: For lolly, I laugh uncontrollably, loudly

indicators.note: said loudly, out loud, these words are heard rather than read

parts.note: uncontrollable laughter is a scream, so this says I scream

explanation.surface: Someone guffaws helplessly in exchange for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lolly' is British slang for money as well as a frozen sweet, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice lolly or an ice cream is a frozen dessert, so the term stands for one.

clue.text: Wife's complaint about misspelt, untrue article

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: letters wrongly spelt are jumbled, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wife grumbles about a badly written, inaccurate piece in the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misspelt' is the anagram signal; 'complaint' points to the old phrase for a wife's bedtime scolding.
explanation.definitionFit: This old term means a scolding given by a wife to her husband behind the bed-curtains at night.

clue.text: 'arlot standing in line in old slum area

indicators.note: the woman stands inside the line

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
a harlot is a hooker; with the H dropped, as the apostrophe shows, she becomes an 'ooker

explanation.surface: A Cockney prostitute stands in a queue in a former slum.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''arlot' signals a Cockney dropped H, so the synonym loses its H too.
explanation.definitionFit: In Victorian London a rookery was a crowded tenement district.

clue.text: Written acknowledgment of right to carry a small part over

indicators.note: the abbreviation carries the other letters inside it
turned over, the word runs backwards

parts.note: a piece is a part

explanation.surface: A document confirming permission to transport a fragment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal signal and 'to carry' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A receipt is a written statement that payment or goods have been received.

clue.text: Express sorrow about girl's rent

indicators.note: the sorrowful word goes around the girl

parts.note: to cry is to express sorrow
Ann is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Lament a young woman's rent payments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rent' here is a split or crack, not money owed.
explanation.definitionFit: A cranny is a narrow opening or crevice, a tear in a surface.

clue.text: Ball game — I quit the match

parts.note: croquet is a lawn game played with mallets and balls

indicators.note: the letter I leaves the word for a match

parts.note: a tie is a match, as in a cup tie
taken as written

explanation.surface: A player storms off from a croquet match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quit' removes I from TIE, leaving TE. 'Ball game' looks like one idea, but 'Ball' is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A croquette is a small rissole of minced food rolled into a ball and fried.

clue.text: Lower of two articles abroad

parts.note: un is French for a, der German for the: both are articles
der is the German definite article

explanation.surface: The lesser of two foreign essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Under means beneath, a synonym for lower.

clue.text: Police with some hesitation come back and come back again

indicators.note: returning, the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: the RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the Northern Ireland police force
er is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: Officers hesitate, retreat and then retreat again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'come back' turns RUCER round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recur is to happen repeatedly, returning once more.

clue.text: Staff kept by newspaperman to do editing job

indicators.note: the word for staff is held inside the newspaperman

parts.note: ED is short for editor
staff are the workforce, the men

explanation.surface: An editor keeps staff on to carry out editing.
explanation.walkthrough: ED for editor is a standard crossword abbreviation for a newspaperman.
explanation.definitionFit: To emend is to correct and improve a text, which is the editor's task.

clue.text: A choice about the time for surgery

indicators.note: the choice wraps round the period

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone chooses when to have their operation.
explanation.walkthrough: The leading 'A' is part of 'A choice', an option, and gives no letter of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure.

clue.text: Fuel found beneath the surface of the earth

indicators.note: what lies below the top letter, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: soil is earth

explanation.surface: Petroleum is discovered underground.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the top letter, S, from SOIL; the surface reading is also literally true.
explanation.definitionFit: Oil is burned as fuel.

clue.text: Can an exam appear magisterial?

parts.note: may means can, as in permission
an oral is a spoken examination

explanation.surface: A question whether a test can look authoritative.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the office of a town's chief magistrate, the mayor.

clue.text: Writer put back opening to play

indicators.note: the opening word is placed in reverse

parts.note: a slot is an opening
to toy is to play

explanation.surface: An author postpones the opening of a play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back' reverses SLOT to TOLS.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy was the Russian novelist who wrote War and Peace.
